senses.sense_definition: The part of a musical wind instrument that is placed into or against the player's mouth.

examples.text: Before playing the trumpet, she carefully cleaned the brass <w>mouthpiece</w>.
He attached a new reed to the saxophone <w>mouthpiece</w> before the rehearsal.

senses.sense_definition: A person, newspaper, or organization that speaks on behalf of another or expresses their opinions.

examples.text: The novel's protagonist often serves as a <w>mouthpiece</w> for the author's own political opinions.
Critics accused the state television channel of being a propaganda <w>mouthpiece</w> for the government.

senses.sense_definition: A protective piece worn inside the mouth by athletes to protect the teeth and gums; a mouthguard.

examples.text: The boxer adjusted his rubber <w>mouthpiece</w> before stepping into the ring for the final round.
Rugby players are required to wear a fitted <w>mouthpiece</w> to prevent dental injuries during collisions.

senses.sense_definition: The part of a telephone or headset that is held close to the mouth to speak into.

examples.text: She covered the <w>mouthpiece</w> with her hand so the caller could not hear her whisper.
He spoke directly into the telephone <w>mouthpiece</w> so that his voice would sound clear.

senses.sense_definition: A lawyer, especially one representing a criminal defendant.

examples.text: The arrested gangster refused to answer questions until his <w>mouthpiece</w> arrived at the police station.
He hired an expensive legal <w>mouthpiece</w> who managed to get all criminal charges dismissed.

traits.comment: Used especially in criminal or underworld contexts
